highlights: The Military Governor proposed the establishment of a Korean legislative body composed of party representatives and elected provincial delegates.
Ordinance No. 97 created an independent Department of Labor and affirmed workers' rights to form unions and engage in collective bargaining.
Ordinance No. 94 established Cheju-do and the Chuja Archipelago as a separate province, restoring administrative autonomy lost in 1906.
The National Police Academy graduated its first class of 55 policewomen on 12 July and its first commissioned officer class on 19 July.
The Korean Red Cross Society adopted its new charter under International Red Cross principles, electing Dr. Kim Kyu Sic as its first president.
A major cholera epidemic reached 7,642 reported cases and 4,878 deaths, forcing quarantines, travel restrictions, and mass public inoculations across South Korea.
Price ceilings were instituted on key commodities, including cloth, shoes, soap, and matches, in an effort to combat severe post-flood retail inflation.
The trial of alleged Communist counterfeiters commenced in Seoul on 29 July, where police repulsed an attempted rescue by sympathizers.

summary: Summation No. 10 documents United States Army Military Government in Korea (USAMGIK) activities during July 1946, reflecting an occupation administration grappling with natural disasters, epidemic disease, and acute economic distress. The month was dominated by the catastrophic aftermath of the late June floods, which disrupted rail and telegraph communications, aggravated severe grain shortages in urban centers like Seoul and Inchon, and spurred popular food demonstrations. Concurrently, USAMGIK combated a devastating cholera epidemic claiming nearly 5,000 lives, leading to widespread quarantines, port closures, and the suspension of mail exchanges with Soviet-occupied North Korea. Administratively, Military Government established an independent Department of Labor (Ordinance No. 97), designated Cheju-do as a separate province (Ordinance No. 94), and proposed an interim Korean legislative body. To rein in runaway inflation, the Military Governor enacted strict price ceilings on essential consumer goods and demonetized type A occupational currency. For historians, this issue provides indispensable quantitative data on retail prices, factory employment, and repatriation flows, alongside an extensive institutional retrospective on the reorganization and training of the South Korean National Police.
